# The Stutz Method Explained: Revolution or Just Marketing?

The video explains Phil Stutz's method, which became known for the documentary produced by Jonah Hill. It shows Part X, two tools of the method, the pyramid of vital force and the criticism of those who say that the method only renames old ideas.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on January 20, 2026 (6 min 57 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aB68xEwx3M

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## Where does the method come from?

The Stutz method is a set of mental, visual and direct health tools, which left Hollywood offices and reached pop culture [00:00]. He became known when actor Jonah Hill produced a documentary about his own therapist, Phil Stutz [00:20].

The video asks if the method is a revolution in mental health or old ideas in a new packaging [00:41].

Stutz created the method by dissatisfaction with traditional therapy. He saw patients spend months or years understanding the past and continuing to repeat the same mistakes [01:01]. For him, understanding the cause of the problem is not enough: lack of immediate action [01:24].

## Part X

The method begins by identifying the obstacle to progress. For Stutz, this obstacle is an internal force, which he calls Part X [01:24]. It is the voice that says it will not work and that it is better not to try [01:45].

Part X acts by judgment, fear, laziness and resentment [01:45]. Giving a name to the enemy makes the struggle concrete [02:06].

## A tool against procrastination

The tools are visual techniques to use when Part X appears [02:26]. The first deals with the tendency to escape pain and discomfort, which leads to procrastination [02:26]. She has four steps:

- Visualize what you avoid, as a task or a difficult conversation, as a dark cloud ahead of you [02:47].
- Instead of retreating, shout from within, with all force [02:47].
- Imagine moving forward and crossing the cloud towards discomfort [03:09].
- Repeat the mantra "The pain sets me free" [03:09].

The idea is to treat pain not as something to avoid, but as the key to progress [03:09].

## Active love against resentment

Stutz calls the place of mind the labyrinth where the person goes through the injustices that suffered and feeds anger [03:30]. To get out of it, Stutz proposes active love [03:30].

In technique, the person closes his eyes, concentrates on the chest all the love he can feel and projects that force toward the one who hurt her [03:51]. The goal is not to forgive or please others. It is getting out of the prison of resentment itself [04:11].

## The pyramid of life force

The tools are at the top of a larger structure, which Stutz calls the pyramid of vital force [04:11]. It has three levels, worked from bottom to top: the relationship with the body (food, sleep and exercise), the relationship with other people and the relationship with oneself [04:32].

Stutz states that taking care of food, sleep and exercise already solves 85% of the problems [04:52].

## Critics

The method divided the mental health community [05:15]. Who supports the practical approach and says that it makes therapy more accessible, especially for those who distrust the therapy only of conversation [05:15].

Critics point to three problems: breaking ethical boundaries, how to make a film with the patient; tools that would be ancient concepts of psychology, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy, with a new name; and the promise of rapid healing for complex problems [05:36].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### The Stutz method replaces traditional therapy?

The video's not responding. He leaves the question: Should therapy heal the wounds of the past or give tools for the challenges of the present [06:17]?

### Why is the body the base of the pyramid?

Because, for Stutz, mental health begins in the body: sleep, food and exercise come before the rest [04:52].

## About the video

Have you ever felt that traditional therapy takes too long to bring practical results? In today's video, we immerse ourselves in the universe of Phil Stutz, the Hollywood star therapist who became a global phenomenon after the Netflix documentary produced by Jonah Hill.

We will unravel the visual and direct tools that promise to turn problems into courage and immediate action.

What you will learn in this video:
Origin of the Method: Why did Phil Stutz decide to break up with traditional psychoanalysis?

Meet Your Enemy (Part X): How to identify the inner voice that sabotages your progress and causes fear, laziness and resentment.

Tools in Practice:

The Inversion of Desire: How to use discomfort to overcome procrastination.

Active Love: The technique to break free from the bars of resentment.

The Pyramid of Vital Force: Because 85% of your mental well-being begins in the body (dream, diet, and exercise).

Critics and Polemics: Is the method really innovative or just a "repackaging" of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy?
